questions.question: A therapist designs an exercise program for a patient rehabilitating from a lower extremity injury. The single most important factor in an exercise program designed to increase muscular strength is:

options.A: The recovery time between exercise sets
options.B: The number of repetitions per set
options.C: The duration of the exercise session

questions.explanation: Exercise intensity (load) is the most important variable for increasing strength.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist implements an aquatic program for a patient rehabilitating from a total hip replacement. During the treatment session the patient indicates how much easier it is to walk in the water compared to on land. What factor is responsible for the patient's ability to walk in water?
questions.explanation: Buoyancy reduces weight bearing and makes walking in water easier.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist instructs a patient diagnosed with rotator cuff tendonitis in a home exercise program. The most important consideration when designing a home exercise program is to:

options.A: Focus the program on the individual needs of the patient
options.B: Limit the length of the program to 10 minutes
options.C: Provide written instructions that detail the frequency and duration of each exercise
options.D: Provide written instructions that detail the frequency and duration of each exercise E. Limit the amount of equipment required to complete the program

questions.explanation: A home programme must be individualised to the patient's needs.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: In effleurage the hands move: Exercise Therapy 17

options.B: In the direction of lymph and venous flow from medial

questions.explanation: Effleurage strokes follow the direction of venous and lymph flow towards the heart.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Concise Exercise therapy/Roshan Lal Meena/1st Ed./Pg. 139

questions.question: A therapist designs a treatment plan for a patient with myositis ossificans. Which treatment would be contraindicated during the acute stage?
questions.explanation: Massage is contraindicated in the acute stage of myositis ossificans.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Transverse friction massage is a valuable treatment technique in a variety of common musculoskeletal disorders. Which of the fllowing statements does not accurately describe the application technique of transverse friction massage?

options.A: The therapist moves the skin back and forth in a direction perpendicular to the normal orientation of the fibers
options.B: A lubricant is used to prevent excessive skin friction
options.C: Fingers that are not involved directly in the massage are used to provide stabilization
options.D: The rate of movement is 2-3 cycles per second and rhythmical

questions.explanation: In deep transverse friction no lubricant is used so the skin moves with the fingers.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Concise Exercise Therapy/Roshan Lal Meena/ 1st Ed./Pg. 152

questions.question: Kneading, wringing, and rolling are all specific variations of which basic massage technique?
questions.explanation: Kneading, wringing and rolling are petrissage techniques.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter:
Cited reference: Concise Exercise Therapy/Peepee/Roshan Lal Meena/

1st Ed./Pg. 143

questions.question: Which type of joint receptor would a therapist expect to be most sensitive to high frequency vibration deep pressure, and velocity changes in joint position?

options.D: Ruffini endings Physiotherapy In Medical Condition

questions.explanation: Pacinian corpuscles respond to vibration, deep pressure and rapid changes in joint position.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter:
Cited reference: Physical Rehabilitation/O'sullivan/4th Ed./

Pg. 138-140

questions.question: A therapist attempts to obtain information on a patient's endurance level by administering a low level exercise test on a treadmill. Which of the following measurement methods would provide the therapist with an objective measurement of endurance?
questions.explanation: Rating of perceived exertion is an objective-scale measure of endurance during exercise testing.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Active repetitive exercises, usually of the ankles or wrist performed to maintain or improve circulation in the extremities are also known as:
questions.explanation: Pumping exercises of the ankles or wrists maintain circulation.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Reliable method of increasing central excitation to stimulate motor units in largest proportion of muscle is by:

options.A: Application of assistance to voluntary movement
options.B: Application of resistance to voluntary movement

questions.explanation: Resistance to voluntary movement recruits the largest proportion of motor units.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist determines the maximum load patient can squat ten time is 240 lbs. The patient's ten repetition maximum should be recorded as:
questions.explanation: A 10-RM is the maximum load lifted ten times, here 240 lb.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapist examines a patient with unilateral lower extremity weakness. As the patient performs hip flexion in supine, the therapist helps the patient complete the full range of motion. This would best be described as:
questions.explanation: Helping the patient through the range is active-assisted exercise.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient is limited to 55 degrees in an active straight leg raise. A therapist should apply the contract-relax technique to the __________ to improve the patient's active range of motion?
questions.explanation: Contract-relax applied to the hamstrings and hip extensors improves limited straight leg raise.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapist examines a patient with a limited straight leg raise of 40 degrees due to inadequate hamstrings length. Which proprioceptive neuromuscular techniques would be most appropriate in increase the patient's hamstrings length?
questions.explanation: Contract-relax lengthens tight hamstrings.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist prepares to instruct a patient in a three-point gait pattern using axillary crutches. The most appropriate initial step to facilitate patient learning is to.

options.A: Distinguish a three-point gait pattern from other gait patterns
options.C: Provide the patient with direct feedback on his/her performance.
options.D: Provide a written handout which illustrates the use of a three-point gait pattern

questions.explanation: Demonstration is the best first step in teaching a crutch gait.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapist treats a patient with quadriceps weakness using repeated contractions. This proprioceptive neuromascular facilitation technique should be applied:

options.B: At the point where the desired muscular response begin to diminish
options.C: At the end of the available range of motion
options.D: Only after a manual stretch to the hamstrings

questions.explanation: Repeated contractions are used at the point where the response begins to fade.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist instructs a patient in a D2 flexion pattern. Which of the following most accurately describes the scapula components of a D2 flexion pattern?
questions.explanation: The scapular component of D2 flexion is elevation, adduction and upward rotation.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapist uses proprioceptive neuromuscular facilitation to increase join range of motion using the hold-relax technique. This technique utilizes an ______ contraction, which is at the end point of the available range of motion?
questions.explanation: Hold-relax uses an isometric contraction at the end of the available range.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapist use proprioceptive neuromuscular facilitation techniques to increase muscular strength. The therapist instructs the patient to actively perform a pattern of hip extension, abduction, and medial rotation. This pattern emphasizes strengthening of the:
questions.explanation: Hip extension, abduction and medial rotation emphasises the gluteal muscles.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Rhythmic stabilization is an ______ technique that can be implemented to increase join stability?
questions.explanation: Rhythmic stabilisation uses isometric contractions to increase stability.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist to improve a patient's lower extremity strength. Which proprioceptive neuromuscular facilitation technique would be the most appropriate to achieve the therapist's goals?
questions.explanation: Repeated contractions are used to improve strength.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist designs an exercise program for a patient rehabilitating from a prolonged illness. Which of the following exercises is indicated for coordination training?
questions.explanation: Frenkel's exercises train coordination.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter:
Cited reference: Physical Rehabilitation/O'Sullivan/4th Ed./

Pg. 730-731

questions.question: A physical therapist treating a patient in supine elects to reinforce active movement of the lower extremity in a flexion, adduction, and lateral rotation pattern. This proprioceptive neuromuscular facilitation technique pattern is termed:
questions.explanation: Lower limb flexion, adduction and lateral rotation is the D1 flexion pattern.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Cooling down exercises are performed for a period of:
questions.explanation: A cool-down lasts about 5 to 8 minutes.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: High intensity and high velocity resistance exercise characterized by a resisted eccentric muscle contraction followed by rapid concentric contraction followed by a rapid concentric contraction and designed to increase the muscle power and contraction is also known as:
questions.explanation: Plyometric training uses a rapid eccentric stretch followed by a rapid concentric contraction.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapist instructs a patient to perform a quadriceps setting exercise. This exercise is considered to be an _________ exercise?
questions.explanation: Quadriceps setting is an isometric exercise.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: What massage technique is commonly used at the beginning and conclusion of treatment and may be used during transitional periods prior to changing massage techniques?
questions.explanation: Effleurage is used at the beginning and end of a massage.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Concise Exercise therapy/Roshan Lal Meena/1st Ed./Pg. 139

questions.question: In axial suspension the fixed points lies:

options.A: Vertically above the joint requiring mobilization
options.B: Vertically above the joint proximal to the joint requiring mobilization
options.C: Vertically above the joint distal to the joint requiring mobilization

questions.explanation: In axial suspension the fixed point lies vertically above the joint being mobilised.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Concise Exercise Therapy/Roshan Lal Meena/1st Ed./Pg. 155
